lines.text: Nobody has ever seen the top of this scale.
Level eight: more than a thousand cubic kilometres of ash. No one has ever observed one.
Yellowstone has done it, two point one million years ago, and again six hundred and thirty-one thousand years ago.
And even for the eruptions we do watch, no instrument gives the score.
Eruption size can't be determined by instruments. It comes from measurements, observations, and then a judgement.
So if nobody saw it, and no instrument can score it, how do we know how big it was? That's level eight, and the full video is linked right here.
